subject: Compliance kickoff: EU residency, SOC 2 & export-control items
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Bauer <michael.bauer@fintech-neo.de>, Anne Keller <anne.keller@fintech-neo.de>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up from today — residency, SOC 2, and export-control items

Hi Michael / Anne,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the candid discussion on where security and export controls sit for FinTech Neo. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary requirement: customer data for EU customers needs to be stored and processed in the EU region.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence required for procurement review.
- Need to initiate your vendor security questionnaire (you said you’d share an XLS) and you have specialists looking at OFAC/ITAR implications for certain cross-border feeds.
- Potential HIPAA considerations for a subset of payment data: you asked whether Redwood has HIPAA controls / BAA options.

Our proposed next steps:
1) We attached the vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (blank copy, prefilled where possible). Please populate the sections specific to your intake and we’ll return answers.
2) Rishi will attach our SOC 2 summary and provide access to the full SOC 2 report under NDA.
3) Internal: I’m looping in Monica (security) and Evelyn (compliance) to help with export-control screening (OFAC/ITAR) and to confirm EU-region hosting, DPA/SCC approach, and HIPAA readiness.
4) Proposed timeline: initial answers + SOC 2 materials within 48 business hours; full VSQ turnaround goal: 5 business days from your receipt.

Would you like us to start with the SOC 2 summary and DPA now, or wait until the VSQ is more complete? Also curious whether you anticipate any ITAR-classified content in the data flows we discussed — that would change the export-control path.

Thanks — I’ll keep this thread for coordination.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0143
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx

From: Michael Bauer <michael.bauer@fintech-neo.de>

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — residency, SOC 2, and export-control items

Jordan,

Thanks for the summary — exactly what we needed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We will fill out the vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx and return it by end of day Thursday (CEST).
- On the SOC 2: procurement needs the Type II report and a short SOC 2 system description. NDA is okay — happy to sign one-way if you prefer.
- OFAC/ITAR: our lead on compliance flagged that some third-party enrichment providers could pull in data with export constraints. We don't expect ITAR on our core payments data, but there are adjacent feeds (trade/FX data) that might require a closer look.
- HIPAA: not the full dataset, but one vendor scope we discussed could touch health-adjacent attributes; procurement asked whether Redwood supports a BAA or has HIPAA controls documented.

If you can send the SOC 2 summary + DPA draft today that would be great. We will also schedule a short call with our compliance lead (Anne) and yours if needed.

-Michael
Head of Procurement, FinTech Neo GmbH

On a related note: can you confirm whether you offer an EU-only hosted option (data & keys resident in EU) or if we would need Redwood Private for that?

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Monica / Evelyn — forwarding the thread from FinTech Neo. Key asks: SOC 2 Type II report + system description under NDA, confirmation of EU-hosted region (data at rest + KMS in EU), ability to sign DPA with SCCs, and help on OFAC/ITAR screening for a subset of feeds. Also a HIPAA/BAA question.

Can you: 
1) Prepare SOC 2 summary + pointer to full report (we’ll request NDA).
2) Confirm whether Hosted (Redwood API) can be contracted EU-resident only (we offer EU-hosted, but need any caveats).
3) Advise on whether ITAR is an outright blocker (I understand ITAR-controlled data prevents cross-border hosting/transfer to non-US persons).
4) Suggest suggested language for DPA + SCC implementation and whether we should propose Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) as alternative.

Requesting ETA: initial response with SOC 2 summary + DPA stub within 24 business hours, and a short export-control checklist within 72 hours.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up from today — residency, SOC 2, and export-control items

Jordan — thanks for the ping and clear ask. Below is what we can provide and next actions from Security/Compliance: 

1) SOC 2 & Evidence
- We will provide a SOC 2 Type II summary today and arrange access to the full report contingent on a standard mutual NDA (I attached the NDA stub and the redacted SOC 2 link to our internal share).
- Attachment ready: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary + control mapping).

2) Data residency / EU hosting
- Redwood offers an EU-hosted option for the Redwood API with data at rest and KMS in EEA regions. For customers wanting contractual guarantees we can: sign DPA with SCCs and include an EU-data residency annex.
- Hosted EU option is available for both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity (no need to move to Private unless the customer requires on-prem or air-gapped restrictions).

3) Cross-border transfers & SCCs
- Our standard approach: DPA + European SCCs implemented; where necessary, we use encryption with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) to reduce transfer risk. We will draft a DPA + SCC Annex.

4) OFAC / ITAR screening
- OFAC screening is part of our sanctions screening guidance; however, ITAR-controlled technical data is restrictive. If the customer’s dataset contains ITAR-controlled data, we will need legal review and likely require Private (on-prem/VPC) or a US-only handling flow with export licenses.

5) HIPAA / BAA
- Redwood has documented administrative, physical, and technical controls relevant to HIPAA. We do offer a BAA for customers with covered data; we will provide the BAA template for review.

Next actions / ETA:
- "redwood_soc2_summary.pdf" and NDA stub: within 2 business hours.
- DPA + SCC Annex draft: 24 business hours.
- Export-control checklist & initial guidance on potential ITAR flags: 72 business hours.

I will coordinate the SOC 2 access and share the DPA draft to this thread. If FinTech Neo wants a quick triage call with our Legal (Evelyn) and Security (me), suggest Wed 8/5 0900-1000 CEST or 1500-1600 CEST.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
